name: Nadia Hayes
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember my mother totaling a stall's takings in song.” On Monday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, Nadia prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I learned sums selling tomatoes. I ran the paper till and earned my first paid shift.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an olive canvas jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Nadia has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Nadia steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: Nadia has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Nadia knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To earn a first paid shift on the counter.
family: Jo Johnson is Nadia’s cousin raised in the same household. Nadia checks the date twice. Jo brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Level with the window*, Jo says, “I delivered a complaint and a cake to the same desk.”
connections: Nadia Holland. Drawings and mental arithmetic keep the lunch queue moving.

reactions.situation: A customer cannot pay until the till opens
reactions.response: Nadia asks the cashier what can safely go on a temporary tab.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Nadia accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Nadia asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
